title: Efficacy and safety of once-weekly semaglutide versus once-daily sitagliptin as add-on to metformin in patients with type 2 diabetes in SUSTAIN China: A 30-week, double-blind, phase 3a, randomized trial

what_it_measured.text: Abstract Aim: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) analogue, versus once-daily sitagliptin as add-on to metformin in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) in a multiregional clinical trial.

dose.text: Materials and Methods: In the 30-week, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator SUSTAIN China trial, 868 adults with T2D inadequately controlled on metformin (HbA1c 7.0%-10.5%) were randomized to receive once-weekly semaglutide 0.5 mg (n = 288), semaglutide 1.0 mg (n = 290) or once-daily sitagliptin 100 mg (n = 290).

route.text: Full details of the inclusion/exclusion criteria are provided in Tables S1 and S2. 2.3 | Drug administration Semaglutide and semaglutide placebo were administered by onceweekly subcutaneous injections in the thigh, abdomen or upper arm, and were to be taken on the same day of the week irrespective of meals.

endpoint.text: The primary and confirmatory secondary endpoints were change from baseline to week 30 in HbA1c and body weight, respectively.
The confirmatory secondary endpoint was change from baseline to week 30 in body weight.
Semaglutide was also superior to sitagliptin with respect to the confirmatory secondary endpoint of change in body weight from baseline to week 30.

reported_results.text: Results: The trial enrolled ~70% (605/868) of the patients in China, and the remaining patients from four other countries, including the Republic of Korea.
